title: Match Acceptance Gated by Player Rank
prompt: You are tracking multiplayer match lobbies where players propose match slots with different start times. Each player has a skill rank (1-5 stars) stored in the players table. For each player, find the EARLIEST proposed match start_time from the match_proposals table. However, only players with rank >= 4 are allowed to propose matches; for players with rank < 4, output NULL as their earliest_match_time instead. Return columns: player_id, rank, earliest_match_time. Order results by player_id ascending. Include all players in the output, even those who fail the rank gate.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE players (player_id INT PRIMARY KEY, player_name VARCHAR(100), rank INT); CREATE TABLE match_proposals (proposal_id INT PRIMARY KEY, player_id INT, start_time TIMESTAMP);

composite_moves: lookup gate attribute (rank) from players table
compute per-player pick (MIN start_time) from match_proposals table
apply gate via CASE: if rank >= 4 keep earliest_match_time else NULL

hints: You need to combine player rank information with their match proposals to make a gating decision.
For each player, find the minimum start_time from their proposals, then apply a CASE statement based on whether their rank meets the threshold.
Use a LEFT JOIN from players to a subquery that groups match_proposals by player_id and computes MIN(start_time), then wrap the result in a CASE checking if rank >= 4.
answer_key: SELECT p.player_id, p.rank, CASE WHEN p.rank >= 4 THEN mp.earliest_match_time ELSE NULL END AS earliest_match_time FROM players p LEFT JOIN (SELECT player_id, MIN(start_time) AS earliest_match_time FROM match_proposals GROUP BY player_id) mp ON p.player_id = mp.player_id ORDER BY p.player_id;

_meta.scenario: a console online service tracking multiplayer match acceptance
